Serve a map

Source: R/serve.R
rr_serve.Rd

Starts a server for an rr_map() in the background of this R session, on host only (127.0.0.1: this computer), and opens the page. It answers while the console is idle: a map waits while R runs something else. rr_stop() stops it. A grid's meta and a geojson layer's data are read once, when the server starts.

Usage

rr_serve(
  map,
  port = 8790L,
  host = "127.0.0.1",
  open = interactive(),
  query = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  verdicts = NULL
)

rr_stop(port = NULL)

Arguments

map

An rr_map().

port, host

Where the server listens.

open

Whether to open the page: RStudio's Viewer when there is one, else a browser.

query

Settings for the first view, in the page's address (list(lang = "is", palette = "deep")).

notes

Opt-in, notes pinned on the map: the path of a .geojson file (in a folder that exists) where the server keeps them, made at the first note; NULL, none. The page then has a Notes group: "Add a note", a click on the map, a text, and the note is written to the file with the features under it; a reply joins a note's thread. rr_notes() reads them in R and rr_notes_add() answers. They are answered only for a page opened from this computer (as localhost, 127.0.0.1 or host), and never in a bundle.

verdicts

Opt-in, the readers' verdicts on features: the path of a .csv file (in a folder that exists) where the server keeps them, made at the first verdict; NULL, none. A layer whose popup has a verdict (rr_layer()) then shows a button for each option in a feature's popup. Each answer is a row added to the file (when, the layer, the feature's value of the verdict's field, the option, the reader's line, the feature's title and place); a later one for the feature replaces it, and an empty answer withdraws it. rr_verdicts() reads them. As the notes, answered only for a page opened from this computer, and never in a bundle.

Value

The page's address, invisibly.

Examples

# Opens a map in RStudio's Viewer (or a browser) when run by hand, e.g. by example(rr_serve)
if (interactive()) {
  harbours <- rr_layer(
    "harbours", "vector", label = "Harbours",
    tiles = rr_tiles_table(rr_example("dansk_harbours"), properties = "SI_HARB"),
    style = list(list(id = "harbours-fill", type = "fill", "source-layer" = "features",
                      paint = list("fill-color" = "#d9822b"))),
    popup = list(click = "harbours-fill", title = "SI_HARB")
  )
  m <- rr_map(rr_section("ref", "Reference", list(harbours)),
              title = "Danish harbours", view = list(center = c(10.5, 56), zoom = 7))
  rr_serve(m)
  # again, opening on the ocean base map (it replaces the first):
  # rr_serve(m, query = list(base = "ocean"))
  # with notes pinned on the map, kept in a file:
  # rr_serve(m, notes = "harbour_notes.geojson"); rr_notes("harbour_notes.geojson")
  # rr_stop() # when done
}
